#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=2120
#   --ntasks=16
#   --nodes=1
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   --mem-per-cpu=1000mb
#   -t 6:00:00
#   --qos=hennig
#   --ntasks-per-socket=16
#   --ntasks-per-node=16
#   -o out_%j.log
#   -e err_%j.log

#flux: --job-name=2120
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 16
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=6h
#flux: --output=out_%j.log
#flux: --error=err_%j.log

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=1000mb
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be placed on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --qos=hennig
# Flux QoS/accounting mappings are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may have different priority/limits than intended, affecting wait time and runtime constraints.

# Omitted Slurm options: --ntasks-per-socket=16, --ntasks-per-node=16
# Flux does not have a portable direct equivalent in batch directives; task placement is typically handled by the scheduler.
# Performance implication: ranks may be placed differently than intended (e.g., spanning sockets/NUMA domains), which can reduce performance.

# Slurm variable $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR is not set under Flux.
# Use the directory where `flux batch` was invoked.
cd "${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"

module purge
module load intel/2019.1.144
module load openmpi/4.0.1

# Slurm used srun; under Flux, use flux-run to launch across allocated tasks.
# Slurm's --mpi=pmix_v3 has no portable Flux equivalent (MPI is typically started via Flux PMI).
# Performance implication: if your MPI build requires a specific PMI/PMIx selection, you may need site-specific settings; otherwise MPI startup may fail or be slower.
flux run -n 16 -c 1 /home/joshuapaul/vasp_10-23-19_5.4.4/bin/vasp_stand > job.log

echo Done

reasons: The resource section uses `#flux: --output=out_%j.log` and `#flux: --error=err_%j.log`; `%j` is a Slurm job-id token and is not a generally valid/portable Flux filename token in batch directives. This can lead to non-unique filenames (literal `%j`) and output collisions across jobs.

Slurm requested `--mem-per-cpu=1000mb` but no memory resource is requested in the Flux resource section. If the site enforces memory scheduling/limits via Flux, the job may be under-provisioned and can be OOM-killed or contend for memory, impacting performance.
issues: The allocation requests `-n 16 -c 1` and the launch line also specifies `flux run -n 16 -c 1`; this is consistent but redundant and can become inconsistent if one is edited later.
The Slurm `--ntasks-per-socket` / `--ntasks-per-node` placement constraints are omitted; performance may differ due to changed rank placement/NUMA locality.

cd $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR

module purge
